name: Crane
desc: An overhead travelling bridge crane working a lattice girder — the trolley traverses and brakes, the hoist drum pays out and winds in, and the slung load swings on the rope exactly as hard as the trolley just accelerated, damping out while festoon cables bunch and stretch along the span.

energy.doc: traverse rate + steel weight + tool glow — faster traverse means harsher acceleration and a bigger swing

scale.doc: crane size — girder depth and span vs frame

density.doc: lattice panel count, festoon loops, load size and rated capacity

speed.doc: how fast the trolley works through its moves

y.doc: girder level — the crane hangs everything below it

drop.doc: how far the hoist can pay out — a longer rope swings slower, like the real thing

anno.doc: annotation density: festoon, SWL marking, sway/hoist readout, span dimension

style.doc: aesthetic: toned drafting film / prussian cyanotype / aged engraved plate / additive x-ray ghost / schematic (the load becomes a free-body diagram: weight vector, rope tension, sway arc)

alpha.doc: opacity — steel line work high in the frame, so it layers politely
